passages.text: This policy applies to all conventional first-lien mortgage applications submitted through the retail channel for owner-occupied primary residences.
This policy does not apply to applications with a principal balance above the conforming loan limit.

Qualifying income for salaried borrowers is the gross monthly base pay, verified by pay stubs covering the most recent 30 days and a written verification of employment dated within 10 business days of closing.

Overtime, bonus and commission income may be included only when a two-year history is documented and the income is likely to continue. Where the documented history is under two years, written approval from a Credit Officer is required.
Qualifying income from overtime, bonus and commission is calculated as the sum of earnings over the preceding 24 months divided by 24.
The maximum back-end debt-to-income (DTI) ratio is 43%. Ratios up to 50% are permitted with compensating factors approved by a Senior Underwriter.
DTI equals total monthly obligations divided by gross monthly qualifying income, expressed as a percentage.

When DTI exceeds 43%, the underwriter must document at least two compensating factors, route the file to the Senior Underwriter queue, and record the decision in the loan file within one business day.
Exceptions to this policy are handled in accordance with the exception handling guidelines.
Reserves must be adequate for the loan type.
